nodes.summary: It is not the case that for every natural number $n$ and every recursively enumerable normal subgroup $R$ of the free group $F$ on $n$ generators, with commutator subgroup $[R, R]$, the conjugacy problem for $F / R$ is solvable if and only if the conjugacy problem for $F / [R, R]$ is solvable: for some such $n$ and $R$, exactly one of these two conjugacy problems is solvable.
nodes.title: Kourovka 12.98(b) has a negative answer

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ and every recursively enumerable normal subgroup $R$ of the free group $F$ on $n$ generators, with commutator subgroup $[R, R]$, the conjugacy problem for $F / R$ is solvable if and only if the conjugacy problem for $F / [R, R]$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 12.98(b) (V. E. Shpil'rain)

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ be the free group on the generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and let $N$ be a subgroup of $F$. The conjugacy problem for $F / N$ is solvable when the predicate on pairs of words $(w, v)$ (finite lists of letters, each a generator together with a sign) that some $u \in F$ satisfies $u w u^{-1} v^{-1} \in N$, with $w$ and $v$ read as elements of $F$, is computable.
nodes.title: Solvable conjugacy problem for a quotient of a free group

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $F$ be the free group on the generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. A subgroup $N$ of $F$ is recursively enumerable when the set of words $w$ (finite lists of letters, each a generator together with a sign) whose image in $F$ lies in $N$ is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: Recursively enumerable subgroup of a free group

nodes.summary: It is not the case that for every natural number $n$ and every recursively enumerable normal subgroup $R$ of the free group $F$ on $n$ generators, with commutator subgroup $[R, R]$, solvability of the word problem for $F / [R, R]$ implies solvability of the conjugacy problem for $F / [R, R]$: for some such $n$ and $R$, the word problem for $F / [R, R]$ is solvable but its conjugacy problem is not.
nodes.title: Kourovka 12.98(c) has a negative answer

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ and every recursively enumerable normal subgroup $R$ of the free group $F$ on $n$ generators, with commutator subgroup $[R, R]$, if the word problem for $F / [R, R]$ is solvable then the conjugacy problem for $F / [R, R]$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 12.98(c) (V. E. Shpil'rain)

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every recursively enumerable normal subgroup $R$ of the free group $F$ on $n$ generators, with commutator subgroup $[R, R]$, the word problem for $F / R$ is solvable if and only if the word problem for $F / [R, R]$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Kourovka 12.98(a) has a positive answer

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ and every recursively enumerable normal subgroup $R$ of the free group $F$ on $n$ generators, with commutator subgroup $[R, R]$, the word problem for $F / R$ is solvable if and only if the word problem for $F / [R, R]$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 12.98(a) (V. E. Shpil'rain)

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ be the free group on the generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and let $N$ be a subgroup of $F$. The word problem for $F / N$ is solvable when membership in $N$ is decidable: the predicate on words $w$ (finite lists of letters, each a generator together with a sign) that the image of $w$ in $F$ lies in $N$ is computable.
